name: The Square Gallery
intro: A white-walled contemporary art space on Battersea Square, set up to give emerging artists a stage and to make contemporary art affordable for south-west London. Morgane Wagner founded the gallery and I designed its identity, shopfront and website. It was one of my first 'real life' official applications.

hero.caption: Opening night, 12 May 2016: queues outside the slate shopfront, with the fascia mark and window artworks.

chapters.label: The brief
chapters.heading: A foot in the door for new artists
text: London has few spaces where new artists can get a foot in the door. The Square Gallery was built to change that: a platform for exciting, affordably priced contemporary work, with artists scouted from the Royal Academy, the Royal College of Art, Goldsmiths and Central Saint Martins.

The gallery launched with a group show of eleven artists, including Sin Park, Gordon Berger and Zokatos, who opened the night with a live spray-painting session the guests could join. The ambition beyond the walls: workshops and classes that reconnect art with the local Battersea community.

chapters.label: 01 · Logo
chapters.heading: A mark named after its square
text: The name comes from the address, so the mark is literally a square: a hand-brushed white frame, rough-edged like a painter's stroke, around widely spaced capitals. Stacked as SQUARE GALLERY LONDON for the window sign; simplified to a clean square icon beside the wordmark on the fascia.
chapters.caption: The window sign.

chapters.label: 02 · Corporate identity
chapters.heading: A design language that steps back
text: A gallery's identity has to frame the work, not compete with it: dark slate, off-white and nothing else, so the art carries the colour. The brushed square doubles as a frame on posters and social, and later became the page avatar. The same language ran through exhibition window graphics, invites, print and social.
chapters.caption: Exhibition window graphics for Nothing To See Here.

chapters.label: 03 · Shopfront
chapters.heading: A front that works on the square
text: The unit at 9B Battersea Square was painted dark slate grey, with the logo in white on the fascia and the services set in small type on the lower window panes, a calm front that lets the window hang do the selling.
chapters.caption: Square icon and SQUARE GALLERY wordmark on the fascia.

chapters.label: 04 · Space & web
chapters.heading: White walls, online and off
text: Anton Borkmann shaped the white-walled space, with warm wooden floors and picture lighting. I carried the same calm into the Squarespace website, which put artists, shows and event photos first.
chapters.caption: Visitors in the white-walled gallery on opening night.
